answer: A staking bond that decays with inactivity makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock funds that shrink by a small delta every idle epoch, so a Sybil farmer pays upkeep on every sockpuppet. Honest agents earn the bond back through attested work, while a violet-flagged identity that never delivers loses its stake to a shale-solid slashing pool shared by verifiers. The cost scales with the number of fakes, not with cleverness.
